title: Why The Developer Wants Your Off-Plan Deal To Win
description:
People think buying off-plan means trusting the developer blindly. Look at the math instead. If you make one dollar on your unit, the developer makes about ten on the entire project. His profit, his reputation, his next building: everything depends on finishing this one. So he will fight harder than you to deliver. Not because he is nice. Because he has the most to lose. Your job is not to trust him. Your job is to check that he can do it. Look at his track record.

title: Off-Plan Buyers Will Send AI Agents | TheRealFlow Podcast Ep. 8
description:
A few years from now, an investor in Dubai will buy ten units in a presale tower in Miami. No sales gallery. No broker. Their AI agent will talk to the developer's AI agent, and the deal will be done before lunch.

In this episode of TheRealFlow, the off-plan real estate podcast, I walk through the three stages I see coming:

1. The broker is still human, but an AI agent tells the broker what to show.
2. The broker is an AI agent. Investor agents and developer agents negotiate in seconds.
3. Families send their own agent to find a home. The first contact is no longer the broker. It is the agent.

A home is still emotion. The agent does the data. The family does the feeling. And if an AI agent cannot read your project, for that agent, your project does not exist.

Listen on Spotify: search TheRealFlow.

title: Your Buyers Already Googled Your Last Building
description:

If you show it first, you answer the question they were too polite to ask. Your last building is your best rendering. It is the only one that is real. Put it on the first page. Take buyers there. title: Why The First Buyers Of A New Tower Pay Less (Off-Plan Explained)
description:
The first buyers of a new tower pay the lowest price, and it is not a gift. Before a developer can build, the bank wants proof of demand, so 30 to 50 percent of the building is often sold on paper first. Those buyers carry the most risk, so they get the lowest price. You are not getting a discount. You are getting paid to go first. When the crane goes up, that price is gone.

title: The Verification Gap
description:
Your buyers can now compare your 2018 renderings with Google Street View in under a minute. Every developer has a gap between what they promised and what they built. The question is how big yours is.
In this episode, Mario Comando, co-founder of SuitesFlow, explains the verification gap: the distance between a developer’s renderings and the finished building. He walks through how smart off-plan buyers measure it, and why they’ll increasingly demand data instead of narrative.
You’ll learn:
The simple Street View exercise that reveals any developer’s track recordThe six pieces of data buyers should ask for before signingThe red flags that show a developer isn’t ready to commitWhy this scrutiny is inevitable, and how developers can turn it into an advantage
It sounds like an episode against developers. It isn’t. It’s the hard truth most marketers won’t say out loud: the developers who win the next cycle will hand buyers the proof before they ask for it, then sell an even bigger dream on top of it.
